title: Two left descents give a reduced dihedral prefix under deletion
statement: Let $G$ be a group (a set with associative multiplication, identity $1$ and two-sided inverses), and let $I$ be a finite set [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set]. Let $i\mapsto t_i$ be an injective map from $I$ to the nonidentity elements of $G$, with $t_i^2=1$, whose image generates $G$. For a finite word $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$ in $I$ write $t_A=t_{a_1}\cdots t_{a_k}$, with $t_\varnothing=1$. Let $\ell(g)=\min\{|A|:t_A=g\}$, and call $A$ reduced if $|A|=\ell(t_A)$. Assume deletion: every nonreduced word has two distinct positions whose simultaneous removal preserves its product. Fix distinct $i,j\in I$ such that $t_it_j$ has finite order $m$ (the least positive integer with $(t_it_j)^m=1$). Let $A_i$ and $A_j$ be the alternating words of length $m$ in $i,j$ beginning respectively with $i$ and $j$. If $g\in G$ satisfies $\ell(t_i g)=\ell(g)-1$ and $\ell(t_j g)=\ell(g)-1$, where these equations are read in $\mathbf Z$, then there is $h\in G$ such that $$g=t_{A_i}h=t_{A_j}h,\qquad \ell(g)=m+\ell(h).$$ For every reduced word $C$ representing $h$, both concatenations $A_iC$ and $A_jC$ are reduced words for $g$. No presentation of $G$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $J=\{i,j\}$ and $H=H_J$. Choose $h$ of minimum $\ell$ among $Hg=\{vg:v\in H\}$; the set is nonempty since it contains $g$, so a minimum exists in $\mathbf N$. Write $h=vg$ and $u=v^{-1}\in H$, so $g=uh$ and $Hh=Hg$. Apply [lem-sfb-deletion-parabolic-coset-length]: all its generator and deletion hypotheses are exactly those of the item, and minimality gives $\ell(h)\le\ell(xh)$ for every $x\in H$. Thus $\ell(xh)=\ell_J(x)+\ell(h)$ for every $x\in H$, and $\ell_J(x)=\ell(x)$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the deletion/minimal-coset argument; compare Chapter 4 Lemma 4.0.14(2), printed pp.120–121 (online PDF; local copy WANTED).

proof.text: Apply the preceding additivity formula to $x=u,t_iu,t_ju$, all of which lie in $H$. Subtract the formula for $u$ from the other two, using the two given equations in $\mathbf Z$. The common summand $\ell(h)$ cancels, giving $$\ell_J(t_i u)=\ell_J(u)-1,\qquad \ell_J(t_j u)=\ell_J(u)-1.$$ Thus both descents persist in the two-generator word metric.

source.place: Agent assembly: subtraction of the three length equalities of step 1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-two-involution-alternating-metric] with $s=t_i$ and $t=t_j$. Injectivity and $i\ne j$ give $s\ne t$, and the other hypotheses are stated in the item. Its metric $d$ is $\ell_J$, since the injective alphabet map identifies the binary words. Its exhaustive list writes $u$ as $1$, an alternating product of length $1\le k<m$, or $w_0$. The first case contradicts a descent, since lengths are nonnegative. In the second case prepend the generator opposite to its initial letter. This gives an alternating word of length $k+1\le m$, which is shortest by the metric lemma, so that generator increases $\ell_J$ by one, contradicting step 2. Hence $u=w_0=t_{A_i}=t_{A_j}$ and $\ell_J(u)=m$.

source.place: Agent rank-two deduction from the complete binary shortest-word classification; comparison with Chapter 2 §1, printed pp.27–29.

proof.text: Substitute step 3 into $g=uh$ and the additivity equality of step 1. This gives $g=t_{A_i}h=t_{A_j}h$ and $\ell(g)=m+\ell(h)$. If $C$ is any reduced word for $h$, then $A_iC$ and $A_jC$ both represent $g$ and each has length $m+|C|=m+\ell(h)=\ell(g)$. By the definition of reduced they are reduced, which proves the last clause for every such $C$.
